questionText:
Suppose the following functional dependencies hold on a relation $U$ with attributes $P, Q, R, S$, and $T$:

$$P \rightarrow QR$$
$$RS \rightarrow T$$

Which of the following functional dependencies can be inferred from the above functional dependencies?
explanation:
Given functional dependencies:
1. $P \rightarrow QR$
2. $RS \rightarrow T$

By applying the decomposition rule on $P \rightarrow QR$, we get:
• $P \rightarrow Q$
• $P \rightarrow R$

Now let's test each option:

• Option A ($PS \rightarrow T$):
Find the attribute closure of $(PS)^+$:
$(PS)^+ = \{P, S\}$
Using $P \rightarrow QR$, we add $Q$ and $R$: $(PS)^+ = \{P, Q, R, S\}$
Using $RS \rightarrow T$, we add $T$: $(PS)^+ = \{P, Q, R, S, T\}$
Since $T \in (PS)^+$, $PS \rightarrow T$ is valid. (Correct)

• Option B ($R \rightarrow T$):
Find the attribute closure of $R^+$:
$R^+ = \{R\}$
Since $T \notin R^+$, $R \rightarrow T$ cannot be inferred. (Incorrect)

• Option C ($P \rightarrow R$):
From $P \rightarrow QR$, by decomposition rule, $P \rightarrow R$ holds directly. (Correct)

• Option D ($PS \rightarrow Q$):
Since $P \rightarrow Q$, by augmentation rule, $PS \rightarrow QS$, which implies $PS \rightarrow Q$. Also, $Q \in (PS)^+$. (Correct)
